implement.approach: Test-first, real SQLite. The new suite seeds a file-backed node:sqlite database (testSupport/sqlite.ts harness over the real DatabaseSync, migrations from src/data/db.ts) with the queue shapes the shipping app produces (repository.ts saveAnalysis / commitPracticeSet / finishSession: shot-first practice set; 50 dependents ahead of their parent across the nextBatch LIMIT 50 boundary; two interleaved practice sets plus an independent shot). A reference drainOutbox run records every durable step (each SQL statement incl. BEGIN/COMMIT via observeStatements, plus each transport round trip). The scenario is then replayed once per step with the process dying right after that step (native connection closed, every later statement/transport call throws; the fake server keeps what it already processed), then restarted from the same file until the queue is empty (<=8 drains). On every createSession/finalizeSession/syncShots call the fake server asserts (a) the parent session was already received remotely and (b) no session.create row for it remains in the local outbox (its DELETE committed) — i.e. 'durably acknowledged'. After the queue empties, every queued row must have reached the server. Steps are covered in CRASH_WINDOW=150-sized `it` cases so each case stays far under Jest's default 30s timeout; the reference test asserts the declared window count is exact so no step can silently go uncovered. Harness-only PRAGMA synchronous=OFF / journal_mode=MEMORY (process death, not power loss, is modelled). Two throwaway mutation controls of src/data/sync.ts (not committed; sync.ts restored, git diff vs BASE is the test file only) confirm the suite detects real ordering/durability defects: (1) dropping the cross-batch queuedSession() parent lookup -> 4 failures ('server never received session', 'session.create row still queued'); (2) committing the parent DELETE before the remote createSession ack -> 3 failures incl. a permanently stuck row after 8 drains.

Cause: stale node_modules missing @sentry/react-native 8.24.0 declared in apps/mobile/package.json; resolved by the documented `cd apps/mobile && npm ci` (no code change). Not a BASE code failure.
residual_risks: The suite's crash model is process death (connection closed, later statements fail); power-loss/fsync-loss is not modelled (harness sets PRAGMA synchronous=OFF, journal_mode=MEMORY for speed). SQLite's own commit atomicity is relied upon for the durability of committed rows.

Fault model 'statement fails but process continues' and concurrent drains across syncRuntime generations were analysed by reading (INFERRED: no dependent is sent unless its parent's createSession resolved in the same drain, so ordering holds) but are not exercised by the new suite.

The fifty-row scenario runs ~415 crash points (~19-22s wall on this machine, split into three ~7s cases); a much slower CI runner still has >4x headroom against the 30s default timeout, no timeout was changed.
AC2 cannot be satisfied as literally written because BASE has no ordering defect; the judge must weigh PROCEDURE step 1 ('do not invent work') against the regress criterion.

Code basis (INFERRED from reading, confirmed by the runs): apps/mobile/src/data/sync.ts:303-326 collects session.create parents for every shot.sync/session.finalize in the batch via queuedSession() (sync.ts:216-231, whole owned queue, beyond the 50-row batch); sync.ts:334-414 sends parents first and deletes the parent row (autocommit DELETE, sync.ts:379-382) only AFTER transport.createSession resolves; a parent whose send or delete failed is recorded in blockedSessions (sync.ts:399-404) and its dependents are held with 'session.pending' (sync.ts:365-373 finalize, sync.ts:434-442 shots) rather than sent; shots are transmitted (sync.ts:485) only after that loop; a crash between the remote ack and the local DELETE leaves the parent queued, so the restarted drain re-sends the idempotent session.create (server upsert ignoreDuplicates, supabase/functions/api/index.ts:2121-2127) before any dependent; nextBatch's last_attempt_order rotation (sync.ts:164-195) cannot reorder because parents are looked up outside the batch and dependents whose parent failed are never sent. The shipping enqueue path is atomic and parent-first (runCaptureAnalysis.ts:1656-1676 / originalAnalysisOperations.ts:1223-1232 call commitPracticeSet then saveAnalysis inside one transaction), so no enqueue race exists either. Consequence for AC2 (kind=regress): by construction it cannot be satisfied — the test PASSES on BASE (exit 0, 8 passed) and PASSES on HEAD (exit 0, 8 passed), so the proof outcome is exit_code 1 / status FAIL, reported honestly; the crash-injection suite is the durable proof the objective asks for and the two mutation controls (artifacts/w02-01/mutation1-*.log, mutation2-*.log, both exit 1) show it would fail on a reordering or non-durable-ack defect. implement.approach: Round-1 finding resolved by diagnosis rather than a source change. (1) Re-ran the r1 suite on BASE_SHA: it passes 8/8, so r1's AC2 FAIL was a missing regression, not a flaky judge. (2) Read apps/mobile/src/data/sync.ts, syncRuntime.ts, repository.ts, api.ts, testSupport/sqlite.ts and supabase/functions/api/index.ts to enumerate every way a dependent could be sent before its parent is durably acknowledged (batch-boundary parents, crash between transport ack and local DELETE, lost acks, interleaved sessions, finalize-vs-create order, transient parent failure). (3) Wrote a stronger real node:sqlite proof (file-backed DB; crash-at-every-durable-step across restarts with fresh connections; lost-ack injection using the shipping ApiError(408,'network.timeout'); committed state audited via an independent DatabaseSync connection so an uncommitted DELETE never counts as durable; 50-row batch boundary; two interleaved sessions; attempt-budget and sync_receipt invariants). (4) Verified the suite is discriminating with three temporary source mutations (all detected; source restored byte-for-byte). (5) The unmodified BASE passes every scenario, so per procedure step 1 no fix was invented. Committed the test alone, ran all acceptance commands, pushed devin/pp/w02-01/impl-r2.
residual_risks: AC2 as written (new tests must fail on BASE_SHA) is unsatisfiable without fabricating a defect; the judge will mark AC2 FAIL again. Coordinator decision needed: accept W02-01 as 'objective already satisfied on base, proven by the new suite' (procedure step 1), or re-scope AC2 to a mutation/adversarial proof (the M1-M3 mutation logs attached show the suite detects injected ordering defects).

The proof models process death (connection closed mid-step, SQLite journal recovery on reopen), not physical power loss with an unsynced OS page cache; durability across power loss depends on the device SQLite configuration, which this package does not change.
The new suite takes ~67s (crash-at-every-step across 4 scenarios); it runs in the AC1 command and mobile `npx jest --silent` — no timeout was inflated, but CI wall time grows by roughly a minute.
